title: Source Session Handoff shared definitions (v1.0)
description: Reusable public-safe definitions for source-session-handoff v1.0 wire objects. These definitions constrain structure only. They do not authenticate identity and do not grant permission, role, membership, runtime admission, or access.

boundedRef.description: Opaque source-attested bound. The ASCII asterisk and whitespace are forbidden, so a wildcard cannot be expressed. Presence does not grant receiver access.

boundedRefArray.description: Non-empty unique bounds. Ascending UTF-16 code-unit order is required on the wire and enforced by conformance tests. Empty, duplicate, and wildcard values are forbidden.

destinationUri.description: Absolute https URI with a nonempty host: a DNS name, a canonical dotted-decimal IPv4 address, or a bracketed IPv6 literal. A DNS label may begin with a digit. A host of only digits and dots, or a label that is a hexadecimal integer, is not a DNS name. No user information, query, fragment, asterisk, whitespace, backslash, empty host, empty port, or port above 65535. Hexadecimal, octal, integer, and other non-canonical IPv4 spellings are excluded. The bracketed form is not an IPv6 grammar; well-formed IPv6, including an embedded IPv4 only in the final 32 bits, is the standards-compliant parser used by conformance. Empty path segments such as /a//callback remain valid. Exact binding is byte-for-byte equality of the original strings and is not URL canonicalization.

pkceVerifier.description: RFC 7636 code verifier: ASCII unreserved characters, 43 to 128 characters. Server-side only. It is not a browser parameter and it is not durable browser state.

pkceS256Challenge.description: Canonical unpadded BASE64URL of the 32-byte SHA-256 digest. The final character is limited to the spellings whose unused bits are zero. The only challenge method in v1.0 is S256.

browserState.description: High-entropy opaque browser correlation of at least 128 bits. It is bound server-side to transaction_ref. It is not required to equal transaction_ref.

authorizationCode.description: Opaque single-use authorization code. The issuer MUST draw at least 128 bits from a cryptographically secure random generator. The maximum lifetime is 60 seconds.
